<reason>A won by staying tighter to the motion as a decision rule: grant-on-request plus the “even if it complicates infrastructure” kicker. A made the clash easier to decide by showing personhood does not resolve who speaks, what “intact” means, or why one community’s request should bind neighbors, while B’s replies (joint boards; courts can still approve pipes later) drifted toward co-management CON already offered and conceded costly delay of beneficial works. B kept a live moral frame on legal-but-lethal permits and irreversibility, but did not rescue the specific mechanism.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s pressure on conflicting river communities and the sewage-plant injunction, then R2’s charge that B’s joint-guardianship answer plus “yes, grant it even then” abandoned the motion’s on-request rule.</best_rebuttal>
